question.problem: Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=2+7\textrm{i}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226152/assets/da91da7425e6a02a202881eb1db3f1049d3f9cd204c0c1793c30e2d95676783b.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $0<      \arg(z)<      \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$ Further,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{7}{2})≈1.29\end{aligned}
$$

to two decimal places.
